_readme: A hand-labelled evaluation set. Three meetings that deliberately overlap in
vocabulary (all three mention 'release', two mention 'latency', two mention
hiring), so retrieving the right one is a real decision rather than a keyword
Questions are labelled with `expect` markers: substrings that MUST appear in a
retrieved chunk for it to count as relevant. Labelling by substring rather than by
chunk id means the labels survive a change to the chunking strategy, which is
exactly the kind of change this harness exists to evaluate.
`off_topic` questions have no answer anywhere in the corpus. They measure the
honesty guarantee: the system must refuse rather than assemble something
Questions marked `paraphrase` deliberately avoid the wording of the segment that
answers them ('basket' for 'cart', 'slogan' for 'tagline'). Those are where a
lexical-only retriever should struggle and a dense one should not -- without them
the ablation cannot tell the two apart, and every configuration scores 1.0.

segments.text: Thanks for joining. Three things today: the Q3 release scope, the payment bug, and hiring.
For Q3 the big items are offline mode, the redesigned onboarding, and push notifications.
I don't think we can land all three before the September freeze. Something has to give.
Let's cut push notifications from Q3. Offline mode is what enterprise customers keep asking for.
Agreed. Push moves to Q4 and offline mode becomes the headline feature for the release.
Next, the payment bug. We had that report of double charges on Android. Rahul, where are we on it?
Root cause was a retry loop firing twice when the network drops mid-transaction. The fix is in review.
Rahul will have the payment fix in review by Thursday and QA runs the full payment regression before it ships.
How many customers were affected? We refunded eleven accounts so far, all of them manually.
Rahul also agreed to write up the incident and send the postmortem by Friday.
Last item, hiring. We have budget for one senior Android engineer this quarter.
That's still open actually. I need to confirm with finance whether the headcount carries over from Q2.
Priya will confirm the headcount with finance before we post the role.
Today is the infrastructure review. Checkout latency, the database migration, and on-call.
Checkout p95 latency went from four hundred milliseconds to one point two seconds after the last deploy.
We traced it to an N plus one query in the cart serializer. Every line item fires its own lookup.
Meera will batch the cart queries and we expect p95 back under five hundred milliseconds.
On the database migration, we are moving the events table off the primary to its own instance.
The migration window is the second Sunday of next month, with a four hour maintenance budget.
We decided to run the migration in shadow mode for a week before cutting over.
Open question is whether the read replicas need resizing before the cutover. Nobody has measured that yet.
Finally on-call. The rotation is down to four people and pages have gone up thirty percent.
Meera will draft a proposal to add two engineers to the on-call rotation by the end of the month.
Marketing sync for the offline mode launch. Positioning, the beta list, and the pricing page.
Positioning is reliability. The message is that the product keeps working when the network doesn't.
We agreed the launch tagline is Works Anywhere and we drop the technical framing entirely.
For the beta we have three hundred sign ups but only forty are on the enterprise plan.
Arjun will segment the beta list by plan tier and send enterprise users a separate invite.
On pricing, the question is whether offline mode is a paid add on or bundled into the enterprise tier.
We decided to bundle it into enterprise rather than charging separately, to drive upgrades.
That still leaves the pricing page rewrite. Nobody owns that yet and the launch is in six weeks.
Arjun will own the pricing page rewrite and have a draft ready two weeks before launch.
